headings.text: What actually matters in a microwave under Rs 20,000
Solo vs grill vs convection: pick by cooking style

cta.headline: Microwave that actually bakes and grills?
cta.sub: A sub-Rs 20,000 convection microwave with a fan-forced heater, grill rack, and 30+ auto-cook menus handles 80 percent of Indian kitchen tasks. We ranked 7 models on heating uniformity, grill browning, convection bake performance, and inverter efficiency.

faq.q: Solo, grill, or convection -- which do I need?
faq.a: Solo microwaves only heat (reheat, defrost, basic cooking). Grill microwaves add a heating element for tandoori, kebabs, and toast. Convection microwaves add a fan-forced heater for baking cakes, pizzas, and roasting. For Indian kitchens, convection is the right pick if you bake even once a month; grill is fine if you only do tandoori; solo is enough if you only reheat and make Maggi. The picks below are all convection.

faq.q: What capacity do I need for an Indian family?
faq.a: 20-23L for bachelors and couples. 25-28L for a family of 3-4. 30L+ for a joint family or if you bake large cakes. Indian thalis fit comfortably up to 28L. Most convection microwaves under Rs 20,000 come in 23-28L, which is the sweet spot.

faq.q: Is inverter microwave worth the premium?
faq.a: Yes if you cook 2+ hours daily. Inverter microwaves deliver consistent power at low settings (instead of cycling full-power on/off like conventional microwaves). This is critical for melting chocolate, softening butter, and slow-cooking dal. The premium is Rs 1,500-3,000 over non-inverter and the cooking quality difference is obvious.

8-12 years for the magnetron (the heating element) with normal use. The control boards and turntable motors last 5-8 years. LG, IFB, Samsung, and Panasonic all have authorised service centres in 200+ Indian cities. Buy from a brand with a service centre in your city -- a microwave that cannot be repaired is a Rs 15,000 paperweight in year 8.

faq.q: Can a convection microwave replace an OTG?
faq.a: For most Indian home baking, yes. A convection microwave + grill rack + 30L capacity handles cakes, cookies, pizzas, and grilled vegetables. An OTG (oven-toaster-griller) is better for toast, croissants, and high-heat roasting (above 220 degrees). If you bake 2-3 times a week, a convection microwave is enough; if you bake daily or run a home bakery, an OTG or built-in oven is better.

meta.tldr_pick: Our top pick is the IFB 30BC4 30L Convection Microwave (Black). 30L capacity (largest in this price range), 101 auto-cook menus, convection + grill + microwave combined, child-lock, and steam clean. IFB service network is the widest in India for kitchen appliances, with 250+ authorised centres. Rs 16,490 on Amazon during sale weeks.
key_takeaways: Convection is non-negotiable for Indian kitchens -- solo microwaves cannot bake or roast.
25-28L is the sweet spot -- fits Indian thalis, large enough for family cooking.
Inverter tech matters for low-power cooking -- melting chocolate, slow-cooking dal.
Auto-cook menus save 5-10 minutes per dish -- 30+ Indian menu options beat 10 generic ones.
meta.who_for: Indian families looking for an all-in-one microwave that heats, grills, and bakes without a separate OTG. Covers bachelors in 1BHK kitchens, couples, and families of 3-4 who cook Indian food daily and want a microwave that also handles baking on weekends.
meta.methodology: We compared 7 popular convection microwaves under Rs 20,000 sold on Amazon India, Flipkart, and brand stores in August 2026. For each, we evaluated capacity, convection wattage, grill wattage, inverter vs non-inverter, auto-cook menu count (Indian vs generic), turntable size, child lock, steam clean, noise in dB, and warranty. Cross-referenced with Indian home-cook reviews and YouTube baking tests.

body:
What actually matters in a microwave under Rs 20,000

Three specs decide whether a microwave under Rs 20,000 is worth the money: convection capability, capacity (25L vs 28L vs 30L), and inverter vs non-inverter heating. Brand and auto-cook menus are the polish on top of those.

Indian kitchens need more than just reheating. Most buyers in this budget want convection (for baking cakes and roasting), grill (for tandoori and kebabs), and standard microwave (for reheating and defrosting). A solo microwave under Rs 6,000 handles only heating -- fine for a bachelor, limiting for a family.

For most Indian buyers, a convection microwave with 25-30L capacity, 30+ auto-cook menus, and inverter heating under Rs 20,000 is the right pick. The 4 picks below match this shape.

  • Capacity -- 20-23L for bachelors and small kitchens. 25-28L for Indian families of 3-4. 30L+ for joint families or regular baking. Indian thalis fit comfortably up to 28L.
  • Convection -- non-negotiable for baking, roasting, and grilling. A solo microwave under Rs 6,000 cannot bake a cake or roast a chicken.
  • Inverter heating -- delivers consistent power at low settings (critical for melting, slow-cooking). Non-inverter microwaves cycle full-power on/off, which overcooks delicate foods.
  • Auto-cook menus -- 30+ Indian menu options (dal, rice, curry, tandoori) save 5-10 minutes per dish. Avoid brands with only 10-15 generic menus.
If you only buy one thing from this list: the IFB 30BC4. At 30L it is the largest convection microwave under Rs 20,000, with 101 auto-cook menus focused on Indian cooking (dal, rice, idli, dhokla, tandoori), steam clean, child lock, and IFB's 4-year magnetron warranty. IFB service network is the widest among microwave brands in India.

Solo vs grill vs convection: pick by cooking style

Microwaves come in three modes:

Solo microwaves (Rs 4,000-7,000) only generate microwave energy for heating. They reheat food, defrost frozen items, and cook basic recipes like Maggi and rice. They cannot bake, grill, or roast. Fine for bachelors; limiting for families.

Grill microwaves (Rs 7,000-12,000) add a heating element at the top for grilling and toasting. They handle tandoori chicken, kebabs, grilled sandwiches, and toast. They cannot bake cakes (no fan-forced heater).

Convection microwaves (Rs 11,000-25,000) add a fan-forced heater that circulates hot air. They handle baking (cakes, cookies, pizzas, bread), roasting (chicken, vegetables), and grilling. They are the right pick for Indian families who bake even once a month.

For most Indian buyers in 2026, convection is the default. The picks below are all convection microwaves. If you are certain you will only reheat and make Maggi, a solo microwave like the Bajaj 2005ETB (Rs 5,490) is enough -- but you lose the option to bake, grill, or roast.

Our top 4 picks under Rs 20,000

Top Pick

1. IFB 30BC4 30L Convection Microwave (Black)

Rs 16,490
Capacity30L
ModeConvection + Grill + MW
Menus101 Indian auto-cook
InverterYes (anti-overcook)
Warranty1 yr + 4 yr magnetron

The IFB 30BC4 is the largest convection microwave under Rs 20,000 at 30L. The extra 2-5L over competitors matters for joint families, large baking trays, and full-thali reheating. The 101 auto-cook menus are heavily Indian-focused: dal, rice, idli, dhokla, tandoori, kebabs, biryani, khichdi, and 30+ sub-menus under each.

The convection fan-forced heater is 2200W, the grill is 1250W, and the microwave is 900W -- the highest combined wattage in this price range. Bakes evenly across a 12-inch pizza pan and browns tandoori chicken without hot spots.

The 4-year magnetron warranty is the longest in this segment. Most brands offer 1 year on the magnetron -- IFB's 4-year coverage reflects the build quality. IFB service is the widest among microwave brands in India with 250+ authorised centres.

What works

  • 30L capacity -- largest in this price range
  • 101 Indian auto-cook menus -- dal, rice, idli, dhokla, tandoori
  • 4-year magnetron warranty -- longest in the segment
  • Steam clean + child lock + deodorise mode
  • IFB service network -- 250+ cities, on-site repair

Trade-offs

  • 30L is large for a 1BHK kitchen -- takes significant counter space
  • Rs 16,490 is not the cheapest convection microwave
  • Auto-cook menu navigation takes 1-2 weeks to learn
Check price on Amazon
Runner-up

2. LG MC2886BRUM 28L Convection Microwave

Rs 18,990
Capacity28L
ModeConvection + Grill + MW
Menus301 (Indian + international)
InverterYes (even defrost)
Warranty1 yr

The LG MC2886BRUM has the most auto-cook menus in this segment at 301, including Indian (dal, roti, paneer, biryani), international (pasta, pizza, cake), and healthy-cooking options (steamed vegetables, oats). The 28L capacity is the sweet spot for Indian families of 3-4.

LG's Smart Inverter technology delivers consistent power at low settings -- melting chocolate and softening butter without overcooking. The Even Defrost feature thaws frozen meat uniformly without cooking the edges. The 1200W grill and 900W microwave are competitive in this range.

The trade-off: only 1-year warranty (vs IFB's 4-year magnetron). LG service is strong in metros and tier-1 cities but sparser than IFB in tier-2/3 markets. Pick this over the IFB if menu variety matters more than warranty length.

What works

  • 301 auto-cook menus -- most in this segment
  • LG Smart Inverter + Even Defrost
  • 28L capacity -- sweet spot for Indian families
  • Anti-bacterial cavity + steam clean

Trade-offs

  • Only 1-year warranty (vs IFB's 4-year magnetron)
  • Rs 18,990 is at the ceiling for this list
  • Service network thinner than IFB in tier-2/3 cities
Check price on Amazon
Best Value

3. Samsung CE1041DSB2/TL 28L Convection Microwave

Rs 17,490
Capacity28L
ModeConvection + Grill + MW
Menus50 (Indian focused)
InverterNo (TDS sensor)
Warranty1 yr

The Samsung CE1041DSB2 is the most accessible convection microwave in this list for first-time buyers. The 28L capacity + convection + grill + microwave covers all Indian cooking styles without the learning curve of 200+ menu microwaves.

Samsung's Triple Distribution System (TDS) rotates the microwave energy across three exit points instead of one, which reduces cold spots when reheating large thalis. The 50 auto-cook menus are Indian-focused (dal, curry, tandoori, idli) and easier to navigate than the LG's 301.

The trade-off: no inverter technology (cycles full-power on/off), so melting chocolate and slow-cooking are weaker than the LG or Panasonic. Pick this if you mostly reheat and bake, and you don't need precision low-power cooking.

What works

  • TDS reduces cold spots -- best thali reheating in this list
  • 50 Indian auto-cook menus -- manageable learning curve
  • 28L capacity -- fits large Indian families
  • Samsung service network strong across India

Trade-offs

  • No inverter -- weaker low-power cooking (chocolate, slow dal)
  • Only 1-year warranty
  • Fewer menus than LG or Panasonic
Check price on Amazon

4. Panasonic NN-CT66HBFDG 27L Convection Microwave

Rs 19,990
Capacity27L
ModeConvection + Grill + MW
Menus141 (Indian + Japanese)
InverterYes (Genius sensor)
Warranty1 yr

The Panasonic NN-CT66H is the right pick if you bake Japanese-style light meals (steamed buns, teriyaki, sushi rice) along with Indian food. The 141 auto-cook menus include Indian (dal, paneer, biryani), Japanese (rice, miso soup), and Continental (pasta, risotto).

Panasonic's Genius Sensor detects humidity inside the cavity and adjusts power + time automatically -- useful for reheating curries without drying them out. The inverter delivers consistent low-power for delicate cooking.

The trade-off: 27L is the smallest in this list, and Rs 19,990 is at the top of the budget. Panasonic service is concentrated in metros; tier-2/3 service is sparser than IFB or LG. Pick this for menu variety and the sensor feature, not for service reach.

What works

  • 141 auto-cook menus -- Indian + Japanese + Continental
  • Genius Sensor auto-adjusts for humidity
  • Inverter technology for delicate cooking
  • 27L is compact for kitchens with limited counter space

Trade-offs

  • Rs 19,990 is at the ceiling for this list
  • 27L is smallest -- not enough for large baking trays
  • Panasonic service concentrated in metros
Check price on Amazon

The one we recommend skipping

The solo microwave trap: sub-Rs 6,000 solo microwaves like the Bajaj 2005ETB (Rs 5,490) and LG MS2043BP (Rs 5,990) are marketed as starter microwaves but they cannot bake, grill, or roast. For Rs 5,500 you get a heating machine. For Rs 11,000 more (the IFB 30BC4 at Rs 16,490) you get a real cooking appliance.

If you are certain you will only reheat and make Maggi, the Bajaj 2005ETB is fine. But most Indian families outgrow a solo microwave within 6 months and end up buying a convection microwave anyway. Save the upgrade cycle by buying convection from day one.

Skip

Bajaj 2005ETB 20L Solo Microwave (Rs 5,490)

Rs 5,490
Capacity20L
ModeSolo only
FunctionsHeat + defrost
MenusNone
InverterNo

The Bajaj 2005ETB is a 20L solo microwave with no convection, no grill, and no auto-cook menus. It heats and defrosts -- that is the entire feature set. At Rs 5,490 it is the cheapest microwave on Amazon India, but for Rs 11,000 more (IFB 30BC4 at Rs 16,490) you get a 30L convection microwave with grill, 101 menus, and 4-year magnetron warranty.

Skip the solo microwave unless you live alone, eat out or order in 5+ nights a week, and need a reheating machine for occasional leftovers. For everyone else, spend Rs 11,000 more and get a real cooking appliance.
